data.title: Dow, S&P 500 fall, tech steadies to end rocky week
data.description:
Key points:
  • Indexes: Dow down 1.18%, S&P down 0.43%, Nasdaq down 0.08%
  • Telecoms down, while tower operators rise on report of SpaceX wireless carrier talks
  • S&P 500 energy climbs, tracking jump in oil prices
  • Investors turn focus to big earnings week, Fed meeting

By Lewis Krauskopf, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi and Ragini Mathur

The Dow Industrials and S&P 500 fell on Friday while technology shares steadied to end a turbulent week for the market-driving AI trade, while investors looked ahead to a busy slate of corporate earnings and a Federal Reserve interest-rate policy meeting.

The Nasdaq Composite was little changed a day after the tech-heavy index suffered its biggest one-day drop since June, as concerns flared over financing costs to support heavy AI investment spending.

Most S&P 500 sectors were weaker on Friday, with the consumer staples and financial groups leading the declines.

Next week, about one-third of the S&P 500 reports quarterly results, including Alphabet , Microsoft and Amazon , three AI hyperscalers whose capital spending forecasts will be closely watched on Wall Street.

"There is still fallout from the questioning of the AI trade," said Kristina Hooper, chief market strategist at Man Group. "There's certainly the potential that we see less invested in an AI data center build-out next year than has been projected. So I certainly think that's giving pause."

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 626.43 points, or 1.18%, to 52,241.55, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX lost 33.51 points, or 0.43%, to 7,629.92 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 21.91 points, or 0.08%, to 25,986.95.

For the week, the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq were on track for modest losses, while the blue-chip Dow remained slightly higher, supported by gains in defensive stocks.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor index edged up 0.6% on Friday, a day after a steep drop. The S&P 500 tech sector rose 0.4%.

Telecommunications stocks fell, weighing on the communication services sector, after a report that SpaceX was seeking thousands of cell sites for a fourth wireless carrier.

Shares of AT&T and T-Mobile both sank more than 6% while Verizon dropped 1.6%. SpaceX shares rose 1.5%. US cell tower operators gained, with Crown Castle up 10% and American Tower up 3.7%.

The energy sector rose 2.4%, hitting a record high. Brent crude hit its highest level since late April, after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concern over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East.

American Express shares fell 3.9%. The company raised its profit forecast as it also announced plans to eliminate 5% of its workforce.

SLB shares rose 6.7% after the oilfield services provider beat Wall Street estimates for third-quarter profit.

Data from the University of Michigan showed US consumer sentiment edged down near a record low in October, as rising prices because of the Middle East conflict soured households' views of the economy.

Market focus remains on the earnings season, with robust corporate profit growth underpinning gains for major equity indexes this year. S&P 500 companies are on track to have increased earnings by more than 32% in the third quarter, according to LSEG IBES data.

The Fed is expected to keep interest rates steady when it gives its policy statement on Wednesday, but investors will be eager for clues about whether the US central bank will hike rates at its December meeting. Wall Street is also increasingly focused on the November 3 midterm elections, which will decide control of the US Congress.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.97-to-1 ratio on the New York Stock Exchange. On the Nasdaq, declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.65-to-1 ratio.

The S&P 500 posted 18 new 52-week highs and 6 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 61 new highs and 299 new lows.

data.title: Treasury Yields Rise, Eurozone Bond Yields Fall Amid French Concerns — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Emese Bartha

U.S. Treasury yields rose Friday but remained near the previous day's lows as investors sought safety from the turmoil in French government bonds ahead of a closely watched interest-rate decision.

The Federal Reserve is expected to keep rates on hold Wednesday and resume a hiking cycle in December, as sticky inflation weighs on consumer sentiment while economic activity remains resilient.

The University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index rose to 48 in October, from a preliminary reading of 46.3 and little changed from September, hovering near record lows.

The 10-year Treasury yield on Friday traded at 4.992%, slightly up from the day before but on pace for a weekly decline, according to Tradeweb. The benchmark yield had dropped below 5% for the first time in a month on Thursday, declining 19.3 basis points in its largest one-day fall since March 2023.

Eurozone government bond yields fell after weaker-than-expected flash estimate purchasing-managers data for October in France, Germany and the eurozone.

The data are a key input ahead of the European Central Bank's interest-rate decision on Oct. 29, when it is widely expected to keep rates unchanged.

Investors' concern over France's fiscal challenges and the risk that high oil prices could dent economic growth have prompted a search for safe-haven investments, benefiting U.S. Treasurys.

"The market has real concerns about the French fiscal situation," said Maria Llerena, director of financial research at Domini Impact Investments.

Focus remains on France, where budget concerns and social unrest have sent the country's bond yields soaring.

The 10-year French OAT yield fell 3.5 basis points to 5.040%, having hit a 24-year high of 5.142% on Thursday, while the 10-year German Bund yield declined 1 basis point to 3.330%. The spread between the two stood at 170 basis points, having jumped to 177 basis points on Thursday, its highest since 2011.

The flash estimate French composite PMI came in at 48.4 for October, signaling a contraction in business activity, from 51.1 in September. Analysts in The Wall Street Journal's poll expected a print of 50.8.

"The strongest political signal came from expectations: Confidence turned negative for the first time in nearly two years, reaching its lowest level since April 2020," Claus Vistesen, chief eurozone economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics, said in a note. "Respondents explicitly cited the forthcoming election and concerns about public finances."

Protests, a government trying to pass a budget and presidential elections in the spring of 2027 "complicate things further," Domini's Llerena said.

Moody's Ratings will review France on Friday. The ratings firm has an Aa3 rating with negative outlook on France, "and there is a significant likelihood of a downgrade," said Jens Naervig Pedersen, director in fixed income and forex research at Danske Bank, in a note.

A downgrade, however, is fully priced in and it should not have a significant impact, he said, shifting the focus onto the outlook for the rating.

"If Moody's places France on a stable outlook, then the focus on the rating should diminish," he said.

Composite PMI data--which measure activity in both services and manufacturing--for Germany and the eurozone were both weaker than expected at 52.8 and 51.9, respectively, albeit still in expansionary territory.

  • Paulo Trevisani contributed to this article.

Write to Emese Bartha at emese.bartha@wsj.com

data.title: Robert Half Shares Surge on 3Q Profit Beat, Improved Hiring Activity
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

Shares of Robert Half surged after the company reported a higher-than-expected third-quarter profit, boosted by an improvement in hiring activity.

The stock was up 22% to $46.07 in Friday afternoon trading. Shares have risen 70% this year.

The talent solutions and consulting company after the close on Thursday reported a profit of $49.9 million, or 49 cents a share, compared with a profit of $42.9 million, or 43 cents a share, a year earlier.

Revenue ticked up to $1.36 billion from $1.35 billion a year prior.

Analysts polled by FactSet were expecting a profit of 47 cents a share on $1.36 billion of revenue.

Contract talent solutions revenue grew to $758.8 million from $746.2 million, while permanent placement talent solutions revenue reached $116.9 million from $110.1 million. Revenue from the company's Protiviti consulting subsidiary fell to $483.5 million from $498.1 million.

"Hiring activity continues to improve, supported by gradually improving market conditions," Chief Executive Officer M. Keith Waddell said. "Demand for risk and compliance consulting services also showed encouraging signs of improvement during the quarter."

Write to Elias Schisgall at elias.schisgall@wsj.com

data.title: Top LNG exporter QatarEnergy in talks to buy US LNG from Woodside's Louisiana plant
data.description:
Key points:
  • Long-term deal could cover up to 3 million metric tons a year for 15 to 20 years, one source says
  • QatarEnergy has also reached 4 mtpa long-term supply deal with Cheniere
  • Woodside's Louisiana LNG plant has 16.5 mtpa export capacity under construction

By Curtis Williams and Marwa Rashad

QatarEnergy is in talks with Woodside Energy to buy up to 3 million metric tons of liquefied natural gas per annum (mtpa) from its Louisiana LNG plant under construction, three people with knowledge of the negotiations told Reuters.

If a final agreement is reached, the long-term deal could see QatarEnergy buying LNG from the 16.5 mtpa export facility for between 15 and 20 years, one of the people said.

Woodside Energy said on Friday it does not respond to market speculation, while QatarEnergy did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

QatarEnergy has been buying LNG on the spot market from US exporters to supply some of its customers due to the ongoing blockage of the Strait of Hormuz as the US-Israeli war on Iran and Tehran’s strikes this year have sharply curtailed shipping.

The company is also a 70% owner of the Golden Pass LNG facility being developed in Louisiana, which when complete will have the capacity to export up to 18 mtpa of LNG.

On Thursday, Cheniere Energy reported it had reached a long-term agreement to supply QatarEnergy with 4 mtpa of LNG. Two million metric tons per year will be sourced from Cheniere’s Sabine Pass facility in Louisiana, and another 2 mpta will come from its Corpus Christi terminal in Texas.

Reuters also reported on Thursday that QatarEnergy is in advanced talks with Venture Global for a long-term supply deal to buy at least 3 million metric tons of LNG per year.

Venture Global and Woodside's Louisiana LNG are the US suppliers with the most uncommitted LNG capacity.

Louisiana LNG is said to be asking for a premium for liquefaction fees that exceed $2.50 per mmBtu and are above the average US market prices because of contract flexibility, offering potential buyers shorter contracts in return for higher prices, two people told Reuters.

data.title: Odisha attracts ₹53,893 crore investment proposals at India Chem 2026, expects 20,210 jobs
data.description:
Bhubaneswar Odisha has secured investment proposals worth Rs 53,893.51 crore during the two-day India Chem 2026 in Mumbai, with the projects expected to generate 20,210 employment opportunities, Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi said on Friday.

Majhi, who led the state’s delegation to the event, made the announcement after arriving at the Biju Patnaik International Airport here from Mumbai.

“During these two days in Mumbai, nine Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) and four expressions of investment intent were signed. These initiatives have brought investment proposals worth a total of Rs 53,893.51 crore to Odisha, which are expected to create 20,210 employment opportunities,” he said.

The chief minister also announced that Odisha will host the event next year after discussions with the Centre and the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), which have agreed to the proposal.

Majhi holds meetings with business leaders

During the Mumbai visit, Majhi held 25 one-on-one meetings with business leaders and representatives of companies, including POSCO India, JSW and Larsen & Toubro (L&T), as well as firms based in the US and the European Union.

The discussions helped the state understand investors’ requirements and familiarise them with the facilities and opportunities available in Odisha, Majhi said, adding that several companies had expressed keen interest in investing in the state.

He thanked Union Chemicals and Fertilisers Minister JP Nadda for his support in facilitating discussions with companies.

Odisha seeks to diversify into chemicals and petrochemicals

The chief minister said the outreach was part of the state’s efforts to diversify its economy from a predominantly metal-based one towards the chemicals sector.

  • Read also: NLC India plans ₹35,000-crore Odisha power plant, explores coal gasification and mineral processing

Odisha aims to build an integrated industrial ecosystem encompassing metals, downstream metal industries, chemicals, petrochemicals and plastics, he said, adding that the initiative would help the state contribute to the vision of an ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’.

NLC India proposes largest investment

Among the major investment proposals, NLC India Ltd proposed an investment of around Rs 36,763.51 crore in the chemicals and power sectors, the largest commitment announced during the outreach.

L&T signed an MoU proposing an investment of Rs 8,100 crore. In all, the state signed nine MoUs involving proposed investments of Rs 51,443.51 crore and received four investment intents worth Rs 2,450 crore.

“Odisha is ready to be a major growth partner for L&T in eastern India. We invite L&T to expand its manufacturing footprint, explore new opportunities in chemicals and petrochemicals, and strengthen its presence in engineering and technology,” Majhi said.

data.title: Gold Tumbles Amid Rising Inflation Worries, Higher U.S. Rate Concerns
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Gold prices have slumped on Friday amid rising inflation worries due to a surge in crude oil prices for the second day due to the potential chances of re-escalation in the U.S.-Iran conflict after the midterm elections in the U.S. in November. Concerns of a possible higher interest rate regime in the U.S. have increased among investors.

Front Month Comex Gold for December delivery has tumbled by $52.30 (or 1.29%) to $4,008.10 per troy ounce.

Front Month Comex Silver for December delivery has also slumped by $1.017 (or 1.85%) to $53.990 per troy ounce.

Yesterday, asserting its claim over the crucial Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps announced that four vessels were targeted while transferring oil and caught fire while three were disabled after they struck sea mines laid by the Iranian military. The U.S., however, dismissed these claims.

A day earlier, the IRGC claimed that two tankers attempting to transit by violating Iran's shipping protocol were set ablaze after they struck mines.

Yesterday, the New York Times reported that the U.S. and Israel are preparing to strike Iranian targets through a short but intense military campaign after the November midterm elections in the U.S. The NYT report also noted that talks with Iran are ongoing.

Speaking about Iran, U.S. President Donald Trump stated that the U.S. forces can exit from the Middle East even now but reiterated that the U.S. wants a long-lasting solution to the crisis and not a temporary peace deal. Trump reasserted that the war has weakened Iran militarily and financially.

Fears of a prolonged disruption to crude oil flows out of the Arabian gulf pushed oil prices higher.

While the U.S. claimed shipping traffic across the Strait of Hormuz is returning to normalcy, Iran's IRGC asserted that the strait remains closed for ships.

Against the backdrop of attacks on civilian and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia by Iran-backed Houthi militants of Yemen and threats of further attacks, U.S. diplomats and their families have been instructed to exit the gulf and return to the U.S.

Saudi Arabia's Aramco ordered the evacuation of its headquarters in Dhahran in the gulf near Bahrain.

In an interview with the Financial Times, U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz stated that the war with Iran could last one more year but speculated that the Iranian regime could come to the negotiating table before that.

On top of the geopolitical risk factor, war-risk insurance premiums and other actions to ensure safe passage of commercial ships that carry oil and energy cargo have added to crude oil costs.

The U.S. Federal Reserve is set to announce its decision on interest rates at the end of its two-day meeting on October 27-28.

Currently, investors are betting on a 10.5% chance of a 25-basis-point interest rate-hike while, the odds on rates being held at the current level stand at 89.5%, according to the CME Group's FedWatch Tool.

The U.S. Dollar Index was last seen trading at 101.82, up by 0.22 (or 0.22%).

While the chances of an intense military confrontation offer support to gold prices, rising crude oil prices tend to prolong inflation and could pressure the Fed to tighten its monetary policy. A higher interest rate environment acts against non-yielding gold, making it costlier for overseas buyers.

Analysts are waiting to watch how events unfold in the coming days.

On the economic front, data released by S&P Global revealed that the composite Purchasing Managers Index in the U.S. decreased to 57.60 in October from 58.40 in September.

While the manufacturing PMI edged up to 56.00 in October from 55.90 in September, services PMI edged down to 57.9 in October 2026 from 58.8 in September.

The University of Michigan's consumer sentiment index was revised higher to 48.0 in October, up from a preliminary estimate of 46.3 but remained at its lowest level in five months.

data.title: TikTok's U.S. entity seeking four gigawatts of compute power -- CNBC
data.description:
TikTok USDS Joint Venture, the entity that operates the social media platform in the U.S., is attempting to obtain four gigawatts of compute power by early 2030 to run its numerous live machine learning tools, according to sources cited by CNBC.

The company also plans a “flagship B2B AI product at the frontier of large-model inference and creative automation,” according to a job posting. Earlier this year, TikTok USDS Joint Venture also said it was “retraining, testing, and updating” its recommendation algorithm, currently running on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure.

TikTok USDS Joint Venture is the entity that was established this year by Silver Lake, Oracle, and MGX to comply with an Executive Order removing China’s ByteDance (BDNCE) as TikTok’s majority owner. Silver Lake, Oracle, and MGX each own a 15% stake in the new entity, while ByteDance holds a 19.9% stake.

Other private investors, including Michael Dell’s family office, own the remaining stake.

data.title: Hansa Biopharma announces positive Idefirix PAES results presented in the High-Impact Clinical Trials session at ASN Kidney Week
data.description:
• The 1-year graft failure-free survival at 12 months post-transplant was 90%, which is clinically meaningful
  • Graft and patient survival were 92% and 98%, respectively  
  • Idefirix was generally well tolerated with a safety profile consistent with previous clinical trial experience

LUND, Sweden, October 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hansa Biopharma AB, "Hansa" (Nasdaq Stockholm: HNSA), today announced that data from the European Post-Authorization Efficacy and Safety (PAES) study of Idefirix® (imlifidase) were presented during the High-Impact Clinical Trials oral session at the American Society of Nephrology (ASN) Kidney Week 2026 in Denver, Colorado. The abstract "FR-OR103 Post-Authorization Efficacy and Safety (PAES): An Open-Label Post-Authorization Trial of 50 Imlifidase Crossmatch-Positive Deceased-Donor Kidney Transplants in Europe" was selected as a Late-Breaking Abstract at the congress.

Renée Aguiar-Lucander, CEO of Hansa Biopharma, said: "The presentation of the PAES study in the High-Impact Clinical Trials session highlights the scientific and clinical relevance of these findings and the potential of imlifidase to address a significant unmet need for highly sensitized patients awaiting kidney transplantation. We are encouraged by the continued interest from the transplant community in the growing body of evidence supporting imlifidase."

Oriol Bestard MD PhD, Vall d'Hebron University Hospital, Barcelona, Spain and investigator for the trial said: "The successful completion of the PAES study provides important evidence in a patient population that continues to face significant challenges in accessing kidney transplantation. These findings add to the clinical evidence supporting the use of imlifidase to enable transplantation in highly sensitized patients with a positive crossmatch against a deceased donor."

ASN Kidney Week is one of the world's leading scientific meetings in nephrology and transplantation, bringing together researchers and clinicians to present the latest advances in kidney disease and transplantation medicine. The High-Impact Clinical Trials session features selected studies considered to represent some of the most clinically relevant and impactful research presented at the congress.

The abstract was presented by Oriol Bestard MD PhD, Vall d'Hebron University Hospital, Barcelona, Spain, on behalf of the PAES study investigators.

Summary of the Abstract

Background

Imlifidase have a conditional approval in Europe since 2020. PAES (NCT05369975) is a controlled, non-randomized, open-label post-authorization efficacy and safety trial, designed to provide comprehensive data to support a full marketing authorisation of imlifidase (Idefirix®) in Europe.

Methods

Fifty highly sensitized (HS) patients who received crossmatch positive kidney offers received imlifidase treatment in line with the mode-of-action i.e. conversion of a positive crossmatch to a negative crossmatch and thereby enabling transplantation. All patients were unlikely to be transplanted under available kidney allocation systems, including prioritization programs for HS patients.

The primary trial objective was to assess graft failure-free survival at 1 year after transplantation. Secondary outcomes at 1 year includes kidney function assessed by eGFR, patient survival, graft survival, delayed graft function (DGF), antibody-mediated rejection (AMR) and safety.

Results

  • The graft failure-free survival was 90% at 1 year after transplantation in patients desensitized with imlifidase (n=50).
  • Graft and patient survival were 92% and 98%, respectively.
  • The mean eGFR calculated by MDRD was 51.04 mL/min/1.73 m2 (n=45).
  • DGF was seen in 40% of patients with a median duration of 14 days.
  • AMR occurred in 56% of recipients; however, no allograft loss was associated with AMR.
  • There were no new or additional safety signals found, and no imlifidase infusions were stopped due to infusion reactions.

Conclusion

Imlifidase enables kidney transplantation with a successful kidney function measured as eGFR at 1 year in patients desensitized. Imlifidase was well tolerated, with a safety profile consistent with prior experience and no unexpected or unacceptable risks observed.

Information about the trial is available at ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05369975

Notes to editors

About highly sensitized patients

Highly sensitized patients have pre-formed antibodies with a broad reactivity against human leukocyte antigens (HLAs). Those antibodies can cause damage to a transplanted organ and potentially graft loss.1 The presence of HLA antibodies means that highly sensitized patients have limited or no access to transplantation, as finding a compatible donor organ

is particularly challenging.2,3 The immunological complexity of highly sensitized patients make them spend a longer time on transplant waiting lists, with an increased risk of dying while waiting for a suitable donor organ.4,5 Across the U.S. and Europe, highly sensitized patients comprise around 10-15% of all patients on transplant waiting lists.6,7

About Idefirix® (imlifidase)

Imlifidase is an antibody-cleaving enzyme originating from Streptococcus pyogenes that specifically cleaves and inactivates all immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibody subclasses, including HLAs. It has a rapid onset and inactivates IgG-antibodies within hours after administration. The decrease in antibody levels creates a temporal antibody-free window of opportunity for highly sensitised patients to undergo transplant, thus enabling successful transplantation from an otherwise incompatible donor.

Imlifidase received a conditional marketing authorization valid throughout the European Union on 25 August 2020 and is marketed under the trade name Idefirix for the desensitization treatment of highly sensitized adult kidney transplant patients with a positive crossmatch against an available deceased donor. The use of Idefirix should be reserved for patients who are unlikely to be transplanted under the available kidney allocation system, including prioritization programs for highly sensitized patients.

The efficacy and safety of imlifidase as a pre-transplant treatment to reduce donor-specific IgG antibodies was studied in four phase 2 single-arm, studies in EU and US, a controlled Phase 3 study in US and in this European Post-Authorization Efficacy and Safety (PAES) study. 5,7,10-11 .

Full EU product information can be accessed via the initial Summary of Product Characteristics found here

Idefirix is exclusively out-licensed for transplantation in EU, UK, Switzerland, Norway, Liechtenstein, Iceland and Middle East and North Africa (MENA) to SERB Pharmaceuticals since July 1, 2026.

In the US, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) accepted the Biologics License Application (BLA) for imlifidase in February of 2026 and assigned a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) action date of December 19, 2026.

About kidney failure

Kidney disease can progress to kidney failure or End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD), identified when a patient's kidney function is less than 15%.12 ESRD poses a significant health burden, affecting nearly 2.5 million patients worldwide.12 A kidney transplant is the treatment of choice for suitable patients with ESRD because it offers improved survival and quality of life benefits, and is cost savings compared to long-term dialysis. There are approximately 170,000 kidney patients in the U.S. and Europe waiting for a new kidney.13

About Hansa Biopharma

Hansa Biopharma AB is a pioneering commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company developing and commercializing novel immunomodulatory therapies to transform care for patients with acute or complex immune disorders. Hansa's proprietary IgG-cleaving enzyme technology platform addresses serious unmet medical needs in transplantation, gene therapy and autoimmune diseases. The company's portfolio includes imlifidase, a first-in-class immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibody-cleaving enzyme therapy, which has been shown to enable kidney transplantation in highly sensitized patients, and HNSA-5487, a next-generation IgG-cleaving molecule that will be developed for Guillain-Barré Syndrome (GBS). Hansa Biopharma is based in Lund, Sweden, and has operations in Europe and the U.S. The company is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm under the ticker HNSA. Find out more at  www.hansabiopharma.com  and follow us on LinkedIn.

data.title: How Staffing Firm Robert Half Is Bucking a Stalling Job Market — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Anita Hamilton

An earnings beat at staffing firm Robert Half on Thursday showed signs of a recovery despite sluggish hiring.

Shares of Robert Half were up 20% Friday to $45 a share after the company beat analysts' estimates for both earnings and revenue for the three-month period ending September. Earnings per share came in at 49 cents versus the 47 cents expected by analysts. Meanwhile, revenue was $1.359 billion, a tad higher than the $1.357 billion analysts polled by FactSet had anticipated.

The bigger win, however, is that Robert Half is seeing growth at all as the broader employment services industry lost around 14,000 jobs in September, according to the latest Labor Department statistics.

But Robert Half isn't your average staffing firm. Much of its business focuses on specialized roles in finance and technology — sectors that have fared better in recent months.

The firm's contract job placement business, which accounts for around 56% of total revenue, had adjusted revenue growth for the first time since 2022. It's also seeing "a meaningful increase in demand" for anti-money laundering and compliance work following recent Treasury Department fines and enforcement actions-such as those against American Express and Bank of America — noted Truist analyst Tobey Sommer.

That work is handled largely by its Protiviti subsidiary, which "showed encouraging signs of improvement," Robert Half CEO Keith Waddell said.

"Recovery is clearly underway," Baird's Marc Marcon wrote in a post-earnings note on Thursday. "Clients remain focused on tech modernization, cybersecurity, and IT infrastructure, and demand trends, and AI should also continue providing opportunities for RHI," he added.

Staffing services benefited from higher demand early in the pandemic before peaking at the start of 2022 and declining for the next three years. But that's starting to turn around, BMO's Jeff Silber told Barron's. What started as a recovery in light industrial staffing has spread to the tech sector, which has also grown as a percentage of Robert Half's business.

"Uncertainty also helps the sector as companies may be reluctant to hire full-time workers but still need labor to help meet customer demand," Silber added.

Things are looking solid for the current quarter as well, with the company expecting revenue to hit $1.285 billion to $1.385 billion and earnings of 36 cents to 46 cents per share. Both figures are well above its results for the same period last year.
